subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw implement true soft-steer as pause-or-abort, inject user context, and resume the same active run, or keep steering limited to supported runtime/model boundaries plus explicit interrupt mode?
rationale: Current main supports boundary steering and explicit interrupt behavior, but the requested pause/resume lifecycle would define new active-run semantics beyond the existing docs and related bug-fix PRs.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering For Now
options.body: Land or refresh the ordinary-message active-run steering fix and leave true pause/resume soft-steer as a separate maintainer-sponsored feature design.

options.title: Sponsor True Soft-Steer
options.body: Define a new runtime lifecycle that aborts or pauses current generation, preserves partial state, inserts user context, and resumes with documented provider/tool semantics.

options.title: Document Existing Limits
options.body: If soft-steer is out of scope, update docs to explicitly route users to interrupt mode for replacement behavior and boundary steering for same-run context.

recommendation.title: Keep Boundary Steering For Now
recommendation.body: Land or refresh the ordinary-message active-run steering fix and leave true pause/resume soft-steer as a separate maintainer-sponsored feature design.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to prior active-run steering work and are the best available owner for the runtime/session-state tradeoff.
